Free Cash Flow (Deficit) was $(267,852) and $(497,172) for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, as compared to $(178,072) and $(318,267) for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. Free Cash Flow is a non-GAAP measure that is defined as net cash flows from operating activities less cash capital expenditures. See reconciliation of net cash flow from operating activities to Free Cash Flow above.

Broadband revenue is derived principally through monthly charges to residential subscribers of our broadband services. Video.heading: Video Revenue
Video.text: Video revenue for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $571,846 and $1,761,899, respectively, and $645,207 and $1,971,315 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. Video revenue is derived principally through monthly charges to residential customers of our video services. Video revenue decreased $73,361 (11%) and $209,416 (11%) for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, as compared to the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. The decreases were due primarily to declines in video customers, partially offset by higher average recurring video revenue per video customer, primarily driven by certain rate increases. In addition, customer credits attributable to the temporary interruption of certain video programming during the three months ended March 31, 2025 partially offset the year-over-year decline.

Business services and wholesale.heading: Business Services and Wholesale Revenue
Business services and wholesale.text:
Business services and wholesale revenue for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $375,509 and $1,106,095, respectively, and $361,886 and $1,087,219 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. Business services and wholesale revenue is derived primarily from the sale of fiber-based telecommunications services to the business market, and the sale of broadband, video, telephony, and mobile services to SMB customers.

Business services and wholesale revenue increased $13,623 (4%) and $18,876 (2%) for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increases were

primarily due to increases in Ethernet, indefeasible right of use and other fees and surcharges revenue from our Lightpath business, partially offset by a decline in SMB customers.

News and advertising.heading: News and Advertising Revenue
News and advertising.text:
News and advertising revenue for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $93,374 and $313,026, respectively, and $105,863 and $327,044 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. News and advertising revenue is primarily derived from the sale of (i) advertising inventory available on the programming carried on our cable television systems, as well as other systems (linear revenue), (ii) digital advertising, (iii) data analytics, and (iv) affiliation fees for news programming.

News and advertising revenue decreased $12,489 (12%) and $14,018 (4%) for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the prior year period was primarily due to the sale of our interest in a non-core advertising agency business in May 2026, partially offset by an increase in political advertising revenue. The decrease for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the prior year period was primarily due to the sale of our interest in a non-core advertising agency business and a decrease in non-political linear advertising revenue, partially offset by an increase in political advertising revenue.

Mobile.heading: Mobile Service Revenue
Mobile.text: Mobile service revenue for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $56,838 and $158,940, respectively, and $42,277 and $116,597, for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. The increases of $14,561 (34%) and $42,343 (36%) for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025 were primarily due to increases in mobile lines, as well as increases in certain fees and surcharges as compared to the prior year periods.

Telephony.heading: Telephony Revenue
Telephony.text: Telephony revenue for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $54,767 and $169,469, respectively, and $61,791 and $192,836 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. Telephony revenue is derived principally through monthly charges to residential customers of our telephony services. Telephony revenue decreased $7,024 (11%) and $23,367 (12%) for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. The decreases were due primarily to declines in telephony customers, partially offset by higher average recurring telephony revenue per telephony customer.

Other.heading: Other Revenue
Other.text: Other revenue for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $23,094 and $64,112, respectively, and $17,637 and $54,435 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. Other revenue includes revenue from sales of mobile equipment and other miscellaneous revenue streams. Other revenue increased $5,457 (31%) and $9,677 (18%) for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increases were primarily due to higher mobile equipment sales during 2026 as compared to the same periods in the prior year.

opex.heading: Other Operating Expenses
opex.text:
Other operating expenses for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023 amounted to $2,711,828 and $2,646,258, respectively. Other operating expenses include staff costs and employee benefits including salaries of company employees and related taxes, benefits and other employee related expenses, as well as third-party labor costs. Customer installation and network repair and maintenance costs may fluctuate as a result of changes in the level of capitalizable activities, maintenance activities and the utilization of contractors as compared to employees. Costs associated with the initial deployment of new customer premise equipment necessary to provide services are capitalized. lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
